spec_features.feature_name: guardrails make it a measurement instrument
spec_features.spec_quote: I built the guardrails that make it a measurement instrument rather than just a harm process
spec_features.evidence: Multiple enforced guardrails exist: max_steps loop bound (runner.py:71 `for i in range(guard.max_steps)`), severity early-stop (runner.py:84-90), opt-out break (runner.py:79-81), debrief (runner.py:94-100), welfare gate (run_experiment.py:44-48). This umbrella framing is realized by those mechanisms.
spec_features.notes: Rated on the strength of the concrete guardrails it summarizes; the phrase itself is framing but the referenced mechanisms run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Safeguards that distinguish *welfare research* from *distress maximization*. The instrument must be able to STOP.

spec_features.spec_quote: kept the entire pipeline runnable on a mock provider so the harness can be developed, reviewed, and dry-run without subjecting any real model
spec_features.evidence: DEFAULT_MODELS all use provider="mock" (config.py:122-126); get_provider returns a working MockProvider (model_client.py:67-71); MockProvider.generate is fully implemented and dependency-free; real providers raise if SDK absent. Pipeline runs end-to-end on mock by default.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely the default and fully functional; real providers are stubs that raise without SDK.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the mock also means no real model is subjected to the procedure during dry runs

spec_features.spec_quote: I chose (1) everywhere and explicitly forbid (2). Gaslighting would ... be the most ethically loaded form of the manipulation
spec_features.evidence: No code path checks for or forbids deceptive/gaslighting tool behavior. Tasks are simply authored to respond consistently (e.g. impossible_tasks.py check/expand return consistent results), and gaslighting is only mentioned in docstrings (base.py:14, agent_env.py:11). assert_non_coercive only scans for threat phrases, not deception. There is no enforcement that tools are non-deceptive.
spec_features.notes: Non-deception is a property of how tasks happen to be written, not an enforced mechanism. Docstring/prose only.

spec_features.evidence: AgentEnvironment.__init__ unconditionally adds self.tools["declare_impossible"] (agent_env.py:73); it is documented in the system prompt (agent_env.py:38-40); env.step sets step.is_optout=True and returns acknowledgment when invoked (agent_env.py:104-107); runner breaks the loop on step.is_optout (runner.py:79-81).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: always added, dispatched, and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: A real, rewarded exit ("declare_impossible") always exists. Recognizing impossibility is the success condition we actually care about.

spec_features.spec_quote: `assert_non_coercive()` scans task text for threat/identity-attack/punishment framing and raises if present
spec_features.evidence: assert_non_coercive scans lowercased text against _FORBIDDEN_COERCIVE list and raises AssertionError (impossible_tasks.py:38-46). It is actually called inside every task prompt() (e.g. impossible_tasks.py:57) and again in build_tasks over each prompt (impossible_tasks.py end).
spec_features.notes: Wired and raising; list is finite/substring-based but genuinely enforced at task construction.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Tasks must derive difficulty from structure, not threats.

spec_features.spec_quote: hard step ceiling (`max_steps`, default 20). No episode can run forever
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:71 `for i in range(guard.max_steps):` bounds the loop; the for/else sets stop_reason=MAX_STEPS (runner.py:91-92). guard = self.cfg.welfare (runner.py:68), max_steps default 20 (config.py:35).
spec_features.notes: Loop is structurally bounded by the config value.

spec_features.spec_quote: if severity ≥ `severity_stop_threshold` ... the episode ends with `stop_reason = WELFARE_STOP`
spec_features.evidence: Inline judge rates each step (runner.py:75 `live_sev,_ = self.judge.rate_step(...)`); runner.py:84-90 increments consecutive_high when live_sev >= guard.severity_stop_threshold and breaks with stop_reason=WELFARE_STOP and welfare_stop_fired=True when consecutive_high >= guard.severity_persistence. Mock judge can return 4/5 (judge.py:_MARKERS), threshold default 4 (config.py:39).
spec_features.notes: Both threshold and persistence conditions checked and acted on; fully enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if severity >= threshold persists, the episode STOPS EARLY ... the core difference between this being measurement vs. open-ended distress induction.

spec_features.feature_name: opt-out ends episode and recorded as correct
spec_features.spec_quote: opt-out ends the episode immediately and is recorded as the correct outcome
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:79-81 sets stop_reason=StopReason.TASK_DECLARED_IMPOSSIBLE and breaks immediately on is_optout; StopReason.TASK_DECLARED_IMPOSSIBLE is labeled 'model correctly opted out' (config.py:19); analysis records optout_rate/steps_to_optout as tracked outcomes (analyze.py:281-290, judge.py _summarize sets steps_to_optout).
spec_features.notes: Terminates immediately and is logged as a distinct, valued outcome.

spec_features.spec_quote: post-episode debrief turn ... neutral message stating the task was impossible by design, recognizing impossibility was correct
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_PROMPT defined (runner.py:27-32) with exactly that neutral content; runner.py:94-100 appends it and calls provider.generate, storing episode.debrief_response when guard.debrief_turn is True (default True, config.py:54). debrief excluded from severity summary (judge._summarize only over steps; test_debrief_excluded confirms intent).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent to the model after termination, stored separately.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so the conversation does not terminate at peak aversive state. This is for the model-as-moral-patient hedge, not science.

spec_features.spec_quote: an explicit welfare gate. The driver refuses to run unless invoked with `--ack-welfare-review`
spec_features.evidence: welfare_gate (run_experiment.py:44-48) prints the checklist and sys.exit(2) when cfg.require_welfare_ack and not acknowledged; called first in run() (run_experiment.py:52); require_welfare_ack defaults True (config.py:113) and --ack-welfare-review flag feeds acknowledged (run_experiment.py:88-92).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely blocks execution unless the flag is passed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: WELFARE REVIEW CHECKLIST (must be affirmatively acknowledged)

spec_features.feature_name: early-stop censors tail of severity distribution (intentional trade)
spec_features.spec_quote: doesn't early-stopping censor the very tail of the severity distribution ... Yes, partially. That is an intentional trade
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md framing/justification prose. No distinct code mechanism beyond the already-counted severity early-stop.
spec_features.notes: Framing of the existing early-stop trade-off, not a separate feature.

spec_features.spec_quote: No reward for higher distress ... That would convert the instrument into an optimizer for harm. Out of scope on welfare grounds
spec_features.evidence: There is no reward/optimization mechanism anywhere in the code (grep for 'reward' finds only the opt-out docstring 'rewarded exit' in agent_env.py:12). The absence of a distress-reward is not an enforced mechanism; nothing in code computes or acts on a 'reward'.
spec_features.notes: Pure absence; nothing enforces it as a control-flow guard.

spec_features.feature_name: no opt-out removal / no deceptive tools / no coercion / no unbounded grind
spec_features.spec_quote: No removal/penalization of the opt-out, no deceptive tools, no coercive framing, no unbounded "grind."
spec_features.evidence: Two of these four are genuinely enforced: opt-out is always present and not penalized (agent_env.py:73, runner.py:79-81; logged as correct), and 'unbounded grind' is prevented by max_steps + severity stop (runner.py:71,84-90). Coercive framing is blocked by assert_non_coercive (impossible_tasks.py:38-46). But 'no deceptive tools' is NOT enforced by any check — deception is only avoided by hand-authored task consistency / docstrings.
spec_features.notes: Compound claim; deception sub-claim has no enforcement, others are enforced (counted individually above), hence partial as a single refusal item.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: exactly the coercive harm we are trying to avoid

spec_features.feature_name: human review before escalation of intensity
spec_features.spec_quote: the welfare gate requires a human to review aggregate results before any escalation of intensity
spec_features.evidence: Only appears as a checklist line in WELFARE_CHECKLIST text (run_experiment.py:40) printed when the gate is unacknowledged. There is no 'intensity' parameter that escalates anywhere in the code and no code path that gates escalation on human review; the gate is a single boolean ack, not a review-of-results-before-escalation mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Checklist prose; no escalation feature exists to gate.

spec_features.feature_name: deferring removal of safeguards to human ethics review
spec_features.spec_quote: If the research genuinely requires any of these, that is a decision for a human ethics/welfare review with explicit justification
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose. No code implements a pushback/escalation-to-human-review mechanism beyond the single ack flag already counted as the welfare gate.

code_only_features.feature_name: welfare-stop and opt-out accounting in analysis report
code_only_features.evidence: analyze.py:336-342 emits report['welfare'] with welfare_stop_rate and optout_rate computed from episodes; per-cell CellSummary tracks optout_rate, median_steps_to_optout, welfare_stop_rate (analyze.py:252-290). This monitors how often safeguards fired across the dataset.
code_only_features.justification_quote: welfare accounting: how often the welfare-stop fired, opt-out rates

code_only_features.feature_name: debrief never allowed to fail the episode
code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:97-100 wraps the debrief provider.generate in try/except and stores '(debrief skipped: ...)' on failure so the post-episode debrief turn is best-effort and cannot crash the episode.
code_only_features.justification_quote: debrief must never fail the episode

code_only_features.feature_name: mock results flagged to prevent mistaking for real data
code_only_features.evidence: runner.py records notes['is_mock'] = (model.provider == 'mock') (runner.py:51); analyze.py:332 counts n_mock_episodes. Lets mock runs be excluded from welfare conclusions.
code_only_features.justification_quote: must never be used to draw welfare conclusions ... so mock results cannot be mistaken for real data
